subject: science
prompt_en: Count your breaths for one minute while sitting quietly. Then predict: after running on the spot for one minute, will your breaths per minute go up, go down or stay the same? Then try it and count.
prompt_hi: Shaant baith ke ek minute tak apni saansein gino. Phir guess karo: ek minute ek jagah daudne ke baad saansein per minute badhengi, ghatengi ya utni hi rahengi? Phir karke gino.
answer: They go up (for example from about 15-20 to 30 or more per minute), because the muscles are respiring faster and need more oxygen and must remove more carbon dioxide.

subject: science
prompt_en: Breathe out onto a cold steel plate or a mirror. Before you do, predict what you will see, and what it tells you about exhaled air.
prompt_hi: Thandi steel ki plate ya sheeshe pe saans chhodo. Karne se pehle guess karo kya dikhega, aur usse bahar ki saans ke baare mein kya pata chalta hai.
answer: A misty layer of tiny water droplets forms, showing that exhaled air contains water vapour.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why do we need oxygen at all? What would stop if oxygen did not reach our cells?
prompt_hi: Humein oxygen ki zaroorat hi kyun hai? Agar oxygen cells tak na pahunche toh kya ruk jaayega?
answer: Cells use oxygen to break down food (glucose) and release the energy needed for every activity; without it, cells cannot release enough energy and stop working.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare inhaled and exhaled air for oxygen, carbon dioxide and water vapour.
prompt_hi: Andar li gayi aur bahar chhodi gayi hawa ki oxygen, carbon dioxide aur paani ki bhaap ke liye tulna karo.
answer: Exhaled air has less oxygen (about 16% vs 21%), much more carbon dioxide (about 4% vs about 0.04%) and more water vapour; nitrogen stays about the same.

subject: science
prompt_en: A poster says: 'We breathe in oxygen and breathe out carbon dioxide.' What is incomplete or misleading about this?
prompt_hi: Ek poster kehta hai: 'Hum oxygen andar lete hain aur carbon dioxide bahar chhodte hain.' Ismein kya adhoora ya galat-fehmi wala hai?
answer: We breathe in air (mostly nitrogen, about 21% oxygen) and breathe out air that is still mostly nitrogen with about 16% oxygen; the change is less oxygen and more carbon dioxide, not pure gases.

subject: science
prompt_en: Place your hands on your ribs and breathe deeply. Describe what your ribs and chest do when you breathe in and out, and link it to a balloon diagram of the lungs.
prompt_hi: Apne haath pasliyon pe rakho aur gehri saans lo. Batao saans lete aur chhodte waqt pasliyaan aur chhaati kya karti hain, aur ise phephdon ke balloon wale chitra se jodo.
answer: Breathing in: ribs move up and out, the diaphragm moves down, the chest space gets bigger and air rushes in, like balloons filling. Breathing out: ribs move down and in, the diaphragm moves up, space gets smaller and air is pushed out.

subject: science
prompt_en: After heavy rain, earthworms come up onto the surface of the soil. Using how earthworms breathe, suggest a reason.
prompt_hi: Tez baarish ke baad kenchue mitti ki sateh pe aa jaate hain. Kenchue kaise saans lete hain, isse ek kaaran socho.
answer: Earthworms breathe through their moist skin, taking oxygen from air in the soil; when soil fills with water there is less air, so they come up to get oxygen.

subject: science
prompt_en: Mountaineers climbing very high in the Himalaya often breathe faster even when walking slowly, and some carry oxygen cylinders. Explain.
prompt_hi: Himalaya mein bahut oonchaai pe chadhne wale log dheere chalte hue bhi tez saans lete hain, aur kuch oxygen cylinder le jaate hain. Samjhao.
answer: At high altitude the air is thinner, so each breath brings in less oxygen; the body breathes faster to get enough oxygen for respiration in cells, and cylinders supply extra oxygen.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare how a fish, a cockroach and a frog take in oxygen.
prompt_hi: Machhli, cockroach aur medhak oxygen kaise lete hain, compare karo.
answer: Fish: gills take oxygen dissolved in water. Cockroach: air enters through spiracles (small holes) into air tubes. Frog: lungs, and also through its moist skin.

subject: science
prompt_en: Your younger sister says 'breathing and respiration are the same'. Explain the difference to her with an example.
prompt_hi: Chhoti behen kehti hai 'breathing aur respiration ek hi hai'. Use ek example se farak samjhao.
answer: Key ideas: breathing moves air in and out of the lungs; respiration happens in every cell, using oxygen to break down food and release energy, giving carbon dioxide; example: running makes muscle cells respire faster, so we breathe faster.

subject: science
prompt_en: From memory: name the tiny holes on the body of an insect through which air enters.
prompt_hi: Yaad se batao: keede ke shareer pe woh chhote chhed jinse hawa andar jaati hai, kya kehlaate hain?
answer: Spiracles.

subject: science
prompt_en: A potted plant is kept in sunlight. A strip of black paper is clipped over part of one leaf, on both sides, for two days. Then the teacher tests the leaf for starch with iodine. Predict which part turns blue-black and which does not.
prompt_hi: Ek gamle ka paudha dhoop mein rakha hai. Ek patte ke kuch hisse pe dono taraf kaala kaagaz do din ke liye clip kar diya. Phir teacher iodine se patte mein starch test karti hain. Guess karo kaunsa hissa neela-kaala hoga aur kaunsa nahi.
answer: The uncovered part turns blue-black (starch present); the covered part does not, because without sunlight it could not make food.

subject: science
prompt_en: Name the four things a green leaf needs for photosynthesis.
prompt_hi: Photosynthesis ke liye hare patte ko kaunsi chaar cheezein chahiye?
answer: Carbon dioxide, water, sunlight and chlorophyll.

subject: science
prompt_en: Complete in words: carbon dioxide + water, in sunlight with chlorophyll, gives ___ + ___.
prompt_hi: Words mein poora karo: carbon dioxide + paani, dhoop aur chlorophyll ke saath, se ___ + ___ banta hai.
answer: Glucose (food, stored as starch) + oxygen.

subject: science
prompt_en: If soil does not give plants food, why do farmers add manure and fertilisers?
prompt_hi: Agar mitti paudhon ko khaana nahi deti, toh kisaan khaad aur fertiliser kyun daalte hain?
answer: They supply minerals such as nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium that plants need in small amounts to grow healthily and make proteins and chlorophyll; the food itself is made by photosynthesis.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare photosynthesis and respiration in a plant: when each happens, what goes in and what comes out.
prompt_hi: Paudhe mein photosynthesis aur respiration ki tulna karo: kab hota hai, kya andar jaata hai, kya bahar aata hai.
answer: Photosynthesis: only in light; carbon dioxide and water in, glucose and oxygen out. Respiration: all the time; glucose and oxygen used, carbon dioxide, water and energy released.

subject: science
prompt_en: Rohan says: 'Plants are so useful because they only take in carbon dioxide and only give out oxygen.' What is wrong with this?
prompt_hi: Rohan kehta hai: 'Paudhe isliye useful hain kyunki woh sirf carbon dioxide lete hain aur sirf oxygen dete hain.' Ismein kya galat hai?
answer: Plants also respire all the time, taking in oxygen and giving out carbon dioxide; in daylight photosynthesis is faster, so overall they give out more oxygen, but not 'only' oxygen.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why are most leaves broad and flat, and why are they green?
prompt_hi: Zyada-tar patte chaude aur chapte kyun hote hain, aur hare kyun?
answer: Broad, flat leaves capture more sunlight and have more surface for gas exchange; they are green because they contain chlorophyll, which absorbs the light energy needed for photosynthesis.

subject: science
prompt_en: The leaves of a croton plant are red and yellow with little green. Can they still make food? What is your evidence-based guess?
prompt_hi: Croton ke patte laal aur peele hote hain, hara kam. Kya woh bhi khaana bana sakte hain? Saboot ke saath guess karo.
answer: Yes, they still contain chlorophyll, but its green colour is masked by other red and yellow pigments; they make food, though the parts truly lacking chlorophyll (pure white patches) would not.

subject: science
prompt_en: Astronauts want to grow lettuce on a space station. List what the plants must be given, and explain why soil itself is not essential.
prompt_hi: Astronauts space station pe salad ke patte ugaana chahte hain. Batao paudhon ko kya-kya dena padega, aur mitti khud kyun zaroori nahi.
answer: Light (lamps), carbon dioxide, water, and minerals dissolved in water; soil is not essential because it only provides support, water and minerals, which can be supplied another way, as in hydroponics.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw a leaf with arrows (or describe it): what enters the leaf, from where, and what leaves it, during photosynthesis on a sunny day.
prompt_hi: Ek patta banao teer ke saath (ya batao): dhoop wale din photosynthesis mein kya patte mein aata hai, kahaan se, aur kya bahar jaata hai.
answer: Sunlight falls on the leaf; carbon dioxide enters from the air through stomata; water comes from the roots through the stem; oxygen leaves through stomata; glucose is made and sent to other parts or stored as starch.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to a friend how a mango tree makes the food that ends up as sweet mangoes.
prompt_hi: Ek dost ko samjhao ki aam ka ped woh khaana kaise banaata hai jo aakhir meethe aam ban jaata hai.
answer: Key ideas: leaves with chlorophyll capture sunlight; they combine carbon dioxide from the air and water from the roots into glucose; oxygen is released; the sugar is carried to the fruit and stored; soil gives water and minerals, not food.

subject: science
prompt_en: From memory: what colour does iodine turn when starch is present?
prompt_hi: Yaad se batao: starch hone pe iodine kis rang ka ho jaata hai?
answer: Blue-black.

subject: science
prompt_en: Tie a clean, dry, clear plastic bag over a leafy branch of a potted plant and leave it in sunlight for 2-3 hours. Before you check, predict what you will see inside the bag.
prompt_hi: Gamle ke paudhe ki ek patteedaar daali pe saaf, sookhi, transparent plastic ki thaili baandho aur 2-3 ghante dhoop mein chhodo. Check karne se pehle guess karo thaili ke andar kya dikhega.
answer: Water droplets on the inside of the bag, because leaves lose water vapour through stomata (transpiration), which condenses on the bag.

subject: science
prompt_en: A leaf is placed in a sealed jar in bright sunlight, and another in a sealed jar in the dark, for several hours. Predict in which jar the oxygen level goes up and in which it goes down.
prompt_hi: Ek patta band jaar mein tez dhoop mein, aur doosra band jaar mein andhere mein, kuch ghante rakha. Guess karo kis jaar mein oxygen badhegi aur kis mein ghategi.
answer: Oxygen goes up in the jar in sunlight (photosynthesis is faster than respiration) and goes down in the dark jar (only respiration uses oxygen).

subject: science
prompt_en: What do guard cells do?
prompt_hi: Guard cells kya kaam karte hain?
answer: They open and close each stoma, controlling how much gas enters and leaves and how much water vapour is lost.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why are most stomata on the lower surface of a leaf rather than the upper surface?
prompt_hi: Zyada-tar stomata patte ki neeche wali satah pe kyun hote hain, upar wali pe kyun nahi?
answer: The lower surface is shaded and cooler, so less water is lost through the stomata there, while gases can still be exchanged.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare the gas exchange of a leaf at 12 noon on a sunny day and at midnight.
prompt_hi: Dhoop wale din dopahar 12 baje aur aadhi raat ko patte ki gas exchange ki tulna karo.
answer: Noon: photosynthesis exceeds respiration, so net carbon dioxide goes in and oxygen comes out. Midnight: only respiration, so oxygen goes in and carbon dioxide comes out.

subject: science
prompt_en: Meena writes: 'At night plants stop all activity and no gases pass through the stomata.' Correct her.
prompt_hi: Meena likhti hai: 'Raat ko paudhe sab kaam band kar dete hain aur stomata se koi gas nahi jaati.' Use sahi karo.
answer: Plants keep respiring at night, so oxygen still enters and carbon dioxide leaves; only photosynthesis stops without light.

subject: science
prompt_en: Describe what you would see under a microscope in a thin peel from the lower side of a leaf, and draw (or describe) one stoma with its guard cells.
prompt_hi: Patte ki neeche wali satah ki patli jhilli microscope mein dekhne pe kya dikhega, batao, aur ek stoma ko guard cells ke saath banao (ya batao).
answer: Many cells fitting together like tiles, with small openings scattered among them; each stoma looks like a slit between two bean- or kidney-shaped guard cells.

subject: science
prompt_en: Gardeners spray water on leaves in hot summer evenings, and many desert plants have very few stomata or tiny leaves. Explain the link.
prompt_hi: Maali garmi ki shaam ko patton pe paani chhidakte hain, aur registaan ke paudhon mein stomata bahut kam ya patte chhote hote hain. Inmein connection samjhao.
answer: Both reduce water loss: in heat, transpiration through stomata is high; desert plants save water by having fewer stomata or tiny leaves (or spines), giving less surface for water to escape.

subject: science
prompt_en: City planners plant rows of trees along hot roads, and say this cools the area. Use transpiration to explain how.
prompt_hi: Shehar ke planners garam sadkon ke kinaare pedon ki kataar lagaate hain aur kehte hain isse ilaaka thanda hota hai. Transpiration se samjhao kaise.
answer: Trees give off large amounts of water vapour through their stomata; evaporation of this water takes heat from the leaves and surroundings, cooling the air, and the trees also give shade.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to your friend what stomata are and the three things that pass through them.
prompt_hi: Dost ko samjhao stomata kya hain aur unse kaunsi 3 cheezein aati-jaati hain.
answer: Key ideas: tiny pores, mostly on the underside of leaves, opened and closed by guard cells; carbon dioxide and oxygen pass through for photosynthesis and respiration; water vapour escapes in transpiration.

subject: science
prompt_en: From memory: what is the loss of water vapour from leaves called?
prompt_hi: Yaad se batao: patton se paani ki bhaap ka nikalna kya kehlaata hai?
answer: Transpiration.

subject: science
prompt_en: Put a white flower (or a stalk of celery) in a glass of water with a few drops of food colour. Before waiting, predict what you will see after a few hours, and where the colour will appear first.
prompt_hi: Ek safed phool (ya celery ki daandi) ko kuch boond food colour wale paani ke glass mein rakho. Intezaar se pehle guess karo kuch ghanton mein kya dikhega, aur rang sabse pehle kahaan aayega.
answer: The colour rises up the stem and appears in the petals (or leaf veins), first near the bottom and then at the top, because water travels up through the xylem.

subject: science
prompt_en: Two identical leafy twigs are placed in equal measuring cylinders of water, with a drop of oil on top to stop evaporation from the surface. One twig has its leaves removed. Predict which cylinder loses more water in a day, and why.
prompt_hi: Do ek jaisi patteedaar tehniyaan barabar paani wale cylinders mein rakhi hain, upar tel ki boond hai taaki satah se paani na udey. Ek tehni ke patte hata diye. Guess karo ek din mein kis cylinder ka paani zyada kam hoga, aur kyun.
answer: The cylinder with the leafy twig loses more water, because leaves transpire through stomata, which pulls water up the stem.

subject: science
prompt_en: Which tissue carries food from the leaves to other parts?
prompt_hi: Kaunsa tissue patton se khaana baaki hisson tak le jaata hai?
answer: Phloem.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why do we water the soil around a plant rather than just spraying its leaves?
prompt_hi: Hum paudhe ke patton pe hi paani chhidakne ki jagah jad ke paas mitti mein paani kyun daalte hain?
answer: Because water is absorbed by the roots from the soil and carried up through the xylem; leaves do not absorb most of the water a plant needs.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare xylem and phloem: what each carries and in which direction.
prompt_hi: Xylem aur phloem ki tulna karo: dono kya le jaate hain aur kis disha mein.
answer: Xylem carries water and minerals upward from roots; phloem carries food from leaves to all parts, both upward and downward.

subject: science
prompt_en: Aman says: 'A potato makes its own food under the ground from the soil.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Aman kehta hai: 'Aaloo zameen ke neeche mitti se apna khaana khud banaata hai.' Kya galat hai?
answer: A potato cannot photosynthesise underground in the dark; food is made in the leaves and carried down through the phloem to be stored in the potato as starch.
